problems: The blind guess (goblet or chalice) does not match The Split Oar. The top reads as a rounded cup, but nothing in the figure reads as a split oar blade with a T-grip.
The blade is a plain oval outline with a notch, so it reads as a spoon or ladle bowl (the second alternative) more than a split oar blade.
The splash stars (6061 and 2762) sit at the far ends of long gold lines and read as stray marks, not spray thrown up by the strokes.
The two T-handle crossbar labels (3909 and 3455) overlap at the bottom, and the top tine labels collide. The labels are unreadable.
The wet-hide binding star (4147) sits where gold lines cross on the shaft, so it does not clearly mark a cracked wrap band.
Gold lines dominate the construction. The blue outline gives a real silhouette only for the blade; the shaft and grip are thin double lines.
output.advice: Redraw so the silhouette reads as an oar. (1) Make the blade a wider, split paddle shape with a clear notch at the top, with tine tips 4906 and 3786 at the two prongs of the split. (2) Put the wet-hide binding 4147 on the shaft as a visible wrap band, a short thick segment, not at a line crossing. (3) Make the T-handle a proper crossbar at the bottom, with 3909 and 3455 at its two ends, and stagger their labels so they do not overlap. (4) Move splash stars 6061 (left) and 2762 (right) next to the blade's stroke sides so the spray fans up and out from the blade. (5) Draw the shaft, blade and grip as filled silhouette outlines, and keep gold lines only as faint construction guides. (6) Shorten or offset labels so none are truncated.
